feature: The speed curve under a clip, with stops you drag
summary: A clip with speed stops now shows its speed curve under it on the timeline, on the clip's own clock, with the mock's 3x, 1x and 0 scale and its four bands. You drag a stop up, down and along, Command-click the line to add one, and a stop can now be a Freeze that holds its frame.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording (Help > Sample Recording).

try.do: Put the playhead at 3 seconds, right-click the clip and choose Speed > Add Speed Stop. Do it again at 6 seconds.
Scroll the timeline down to the Speed curve under the clip.
Drag the second diamond straight up to about 2.5x and watch the readout, the curve and the picture follow your hand.
Let go: the stretch around it turns pink (Fast) and the clip gets shorter. Press Command-Z once to undo the whole drag.
Pick the third stop and choose Freeze in the panel's Speed list.
Drag the freeze's second zero diamond to the right to make the hold longer.
Command-click the line to add a stop; right-click a stop for Freeze and Delete Speed Stop.

evaluate: Does dragging a stop feel direct enough that you would reach for the curve before the panel's Speed list?
Are the band colours along the floor and under the line easy to read at a glance, or is the wash under the line too heavy?
Is Freeze from the Speed list, held one second with a second diamond for its end, the freeze you expected?
At the default window size the timeline shows the clip or its curve, not both: is scrolling acceptable, or should the curve get shorter or the timeline taller when it opens?
Reel: 2026-10-17-speed-curve-reel.gif (and .mp4, contact sheet 2026-10-17-speed-curve-reel-contact.png). Is the motion of a dragged stop what you want?
rough: The app beside the mock (video-speed.html, timeline dock) in one picture, 2026-10-17-speed-curve-beside-the-mock.png: it matches apart from the lines below.

Differs from the mock: the clip bar itself is not yet tinted by band and the Slow-mo / Normal / Fast / Freeze legend is not drawn under it; the bands are on the curve instead. Task a-ramped-clip-s-bar-is-tinted-by-its-speed-bands.

Differs from the mock: the curve's name sits in the track gutter beside the plot, like the Zoom and Source lanes, not as a SPEED CURVE heading above it. Task a-ramped-clip-s-bar-is-tinted-by-its-speed-bands settles where it goes.

Goes further than the mock: the 1x label sits on its dashed line (the mock spaces its three labels evenly, which puts 1x half way up a 0 to 3x scale), and the wash under the line is tinted by band rather than one cyan.
The mock's Playhead 1.00x @ 0.00s pill is left out: your call on 2026-09-25 that pills like it are unprofessional (UX-PATTERNS §4).
A plain click on the curve picks and a Command-click adds a stop, the rule every animated line follows (your call on 2026-10-13); the task asked for a plain click to add.
Matches the mock's narrow plot height (104pt) at every window size; on a 1280 by 800 window the timeline shows about 106pt of tracks, so the curve opening scrolls the clip mostly out of sight.
A freeze is one stop that holds its frame, its second diamond the end of the hold, because stops are pinned to frames of the recording; it matches the mock's two zeros on screen.
Matches the mock's scale, which ends at 3x, so a stop dragged on the curve stops at 3x; 4x, 10x and 30x are still in the Speed list.
Cutting a clip in the middle of a freeze restarts the hold and drops the end of the recording: task cutting-a-clip-in-the-middle-of-a-speed-stop-fre.
